jurisdictions.name: Mauritius
jurisdictions.note: A mixed system: the Code Civil Mauricien supplies succession and adult protection, while the Curatelle Act, Mental Health Care Act and Succession and Wills Act are English-language statutes layered over it — the Mental Health Care Act reaches a patient’s property by having the Ministère Public apply for an ouverture de tutelle under the Code. Succession vests without a grant: the heirs are seised of plein droit. No organ-donation role is recorded: the Human Tissue (Removal, Preservation and Transplant) Act 2006 commences by proclamation and the revised-laws editorial note states that, as at 30 September 2007, only section 16 had come into operation, so the donation regime is enacted but not in force on the face of the published text. Powers of attorney and health-care proxies were not located in the Acts retrieved and are not recorded.
jurisdictions.label: Mauritius

jurisdictions.name: Rwanda
jurisdictions.note: Law nº 71/2024 of 26/06/2024 governing persons and family, which carries both adult guardianship (Chapter VII) and succession (Chapter XVII) in one statute and replaces the 2016 law. Published in the trilingual Official Gazette; the English version is quoted here, alongside Kinyarwanda and French. Estate administration runs through a succession council that chooses, supervises and signs off a liquidator, so no role here matches an executor acting alone. Powers of attorney, health-care proxies and organ donation were not found in this Law and are not recorded; they would sit in other legislation not retrieved for this entry.
jurisdictions.label: Rwanda

jurisdictions.name: South Africa
jurisdictions.note: South African estate administration, curatorship and health decision-making: Administration of Estates Act 66 of 1965, Intestate Succession Act 81 of 1987 and Wills Act 7 of 1953 from the Department of Justice, with the National Health Act 61 of 2003 and Mental Health Care Act 17 of 2002 from the Government Printer. There is no enduring power of attorney: a power of attorney is common law and lapses on the grantor’s incapacity, so the written health mandate under National Health Act s 7 is the only advance appointment recorded here. Two statutory routes run in parallel for property — curatorship under the Administration of Estates Act and an administrator under the Mental Health Care Act. The Mental Health Care Act citations carry no quote because the Government Printer’s scan has a damaged text layer; the sections were read but are not reproduced verbatim.
jurisdictions.label: South Africa

jurisdictions.name: China
jurisdictions.note: Roles under the Civil Code of the People’s Republic of China, in force 1 January 2021, with the Trust Law, the Personal Information Protection Law, the Mental Health Law and the 2024 Regulations on Human Organ Donation and Transplantation. Mainland China only: Hong Kong and Macau keep their own systems, and Taiwan is outside this file. Text from the NPC National Database of Laws and Regulations.
jurisdictions.label: China

jurisdictions.name: India
jurisdictions.note: Central Acts only. Succession in India is religion-dependent: the Indian Succession Act’s probate requirement does not apply to wills made by Muslims or Indian Christians, and property passing by survivorship does not vest in an executor, so intestate heirship (Hindu Succession Act 1956 and uncodified Muslim personal law) is not modelled here. The Guardians and Wards Act 1890 is omitted as it concerns minors. No digital-assets fiduciary statute was found in the Acts retrieved.
jurisdictions.label: India

jurisdictions.name: Japan
jurisdictions.note: Civil Code (民法) and the Act on Voluntary Guardianship Contracts (任意後見契約に関する法律), quoted from the Japanese original published by e-Gov. The official English translation stops short of the inheritance book, so the Japanese text is the source here and English role names are descriptive glosses. Japan runs three statutory tiers by degree of impairment — 後見, 保佐, 補助 — which the Code keeps mutually exclusive, alongside a voluntary guardianship contract that only takes effect when the Family Court appoints a supervisor. There is no grant of representation: inheritance commences on death. Health-care proxies, organ donation and disposal of remains sit outside these two statutes and are not recorded.
jurisdictions.label: Japan

jurisdictions.name: Singapore
jurisdictions.note: Mental Capacity Act 2008, Probate and Administration Act 1934 and Human Organ Transplant Act 1987, from Singapore Statutes Online. The lasting power of attorney follows the England and Wales model but is stricter at the front: the Act says the power is not created at all unless the instrument is made and registered. Organ donation runs the other way from most of this set — consent is presumed and a registered objection is what blocks removal. Advance medical directives and disposal of remains sit in other statutes not retrieved for this entry.
jurisdictions.label: Singapore

jurisdictions.name: South Korea
jurisdictions.note: Civil Act roles only. Korea has no grant of representation: inheritance commences by death and vests in the heir. The 2011 amendment (Act No. 10429) replaced incompetency declarations with a three-tier court guardianship — adult, limited and specific — plus a voluntary guardianship contract. Statutory text is the Korea Legislation Research Institute English translation; the Korean original governs.
jurisdictions.label: South Korea

jurisdictions.name: Denmark
jurisdictions.note: Danish national law: Arveloven, Lov om fremtidsfuldmagter, Værgemålsloven, Dødsboskifteloven and Sundhedsloven. retsinformation.dk serves these only as a JavaScript application, so each act was read by rendering the official page; the acts are cited as passed, and each page also lists the consolidating LBK versions.
jurisdictions.label: Denmark

jurisdictions.name: Finland
jurisdictions.note: Finnish national law: Laki edunvalvontavaltuutuksesta 648/2007, Laki holhoustoimesta 442/1999, Perintökaari 40/1965, Laki potilaan asemasta ja oikeuksista 785/1992 and Laki 101/2001 on medical use of organs and tissues.
jurisdictions.label: Finland

jurisdictions.name: France
jurisdictions.note: French national law from the Code civil, the Code de la santé publique and Loi n° 78-17 du 6 janvier 1978, retrieved through the official Légifrance API on PISTE and cited to the public Légifrance URL for each article. France is the only jurisdiction in this set with an express statutory regime for the fate of personal data after death: art. 85 of Loi 78-17 lets a person leave binding directives and name someone to execute them, voids terms-of-service clauses that cut across it, and obliges online services to offer users a post-mortem choice.
jurisdictions.label: France

jurisdictions.name: Germany — federal law
jurisdictions.note: Federal German law: BGB (agency, Betreuung, succession, medical records), TPG (organ donation), SGB I and AO. Burial and disposition of remains are Länder law and are not covered here.
jurisdictions.label: Germany — federal law

jurisdictions.name: Ireland
jurisdictions.note: Irish law under the Assisted Decision-Making (Capacity) Act 2015, commenced 26 April 2023 by S.I. Nos. 192 and 193 of 2023, together with the Succession Act 1965 and the Human Tissue Act 2024. The 2015 Act abolished wardship prospectively and replaced it with three graded tiers. Sections 61, 62 and 70 were repealed on 26 April 2023 by the 2022 Amendment Act rather than left uncommenced, which is why the commencement orders carve them out.
jurisdictions.label: Ireland

jurisdictions.name: Italy
jurisdictions.note: Roles under the Codice civile, the 2017 law on informed consent and advance directives, the 1999 organ transplant law and the privacy code as adapted to the GDPR. Text from Normattiva, the official consolidated portal; each citation records the date its wording took effect.
jurisdictions.label: Italy

jurisdictions.name: Netherlands
jurisdictions.note: Dutch national law from the Burgerlijk Wetboek (Books 1, 3, 4 and 7) and the Wet op de orgaandonatie, as in force on the dates shown by wetten.overheid.nl. Adult protection is split three ways rather than unified: curatele reaches person and property, beschermingsbewind only property, mentorschap only interests of a non-property nature, so one person may be under two measures with different holders.
jurisdictions.label: Netherlands

jurisdictions.name: Spain — state law
jurisdictions.note: Spanish state law: Código Civil as amended by Ley 8/2021 (support measures and preventive powers), Ley 41/2002 (patient autonomy) and Ley 30/1979 (organ donation). Catalonia, Aragón, Navarre, the Basque Country, Galicia and the Balearics have their own civil law of succession, which is not covered here.
jurisdictions.label: Spain — state law

jurisdictions.name: Sweden
jurisdictions.note: Swedish national law: Lag (2017:310) om framtidsfullmakter, Ärvdabalk (1958:637), Föräldrabalk (1949:381) and Lag (1995:831) om transplantation m.m. Who may decide on disposal of the body is not covered: Begravningslag (1990:1144) was searched and no provision assigning that decision was located.
jurisdictions.label: Sweden

jurisdictions.name: England & Wales
jurisdictions.note: Capacity, attorney, deputy, succession, disposal of remains and organ donation law for England and Wales, as in force on 2026-09-16. Differences between England and Wales (organ donation) are noted.
jurisdictions.label: UK — England & Wales

jurisdictions.name: Northern Ireland

jurisdictions.label: UK — Northern Ireland

jurisdictions.name: Scotland
jurisdictions.note: Scottish (devolved) roles for incapacity, death and estate administration, as in force on 2026-09-16. UK-wide roles (DWP appointees, UK GDPR, Access to Health Records Act 1990) are in the uk-national layer.
jurisdictions.label: UK — Scotland

jurisdictions.name: British Columbia
jurisdictions.note: British Columbia provincial roles for incapacity, death and estate administration: enduring and general powers of attorney, representation agreements, temporary substitute decision makers, committees and statutory property guardians, executors and administrators under WESA, organ donation consent, control of disposition of remains, and access to a deceased person's records. jurisdictions.name: Ontario
jurisdictions.note: Ontario provincial roles for incapacity, death and estates as in force on 2026-09-16 (e-Laws currency date 11 Sept 2026). Federal benefit, tax and privacy roles are in ca-federal.json.
jurisdictions.label: Canada — Ontario

jurisdictions.name: Québec
jurisdictions.note: Québec civil-law roles for incapacity, death and liquidation of successions under the Civil Code of Québec (CCQ) and Code of Civil Procedure (CCP), as amended by S.Q. 2020, c. 11 (in force 1 November 2022). jurisdictions.label: Canada — Québec

jurisdictions.name: Mexico — federal law

Organ donation (Ley General de Salud) and disposal of remains are not covered here.
jurisdictions.label: Mexico — federal law

jurisdictions.name: US — uniform/model law + federal

jurisdictions.label: US — uniform/model law + federal

jurisdictions.name: Louisiana
jurisdictions.note: Louisiana is a civil-law jurisdiction. jurisdictions.label: US — Louisiana

jurisdictions.name: Maine
jurisdictions.note: Maine is the closest state in this set to the uniform baseline: it enacted the Uniform Guardianship, Conservatorship and Other Protective Arrangements Act, the act the us-model baseline follows, and is one of only four states to have done so. jurisdictions.label: US — Maine

jurisdictions.name: Massachusetts
jurisdictions.note: No state-specific disposition-of-remains role: no Massachusetts statute setting a right-of-disposition priority was found, so none is asserted.
jurisdictions.label: US — Massachusetts

jurisdictions.name: New South Wales
jurisdictions.note: NSW state roles as in force on 2026-09-16; Commonwealth nominee, My Health Record, tax and Privacy Act features are in au-commonwealth.
